key_insight: Ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM) significantly boosts the hardness and wear resistance of WC–Co–Cr thermal spray coatings, with the best overall outcome depending on the damage mode and spray process.
engineering_relevance: For wear-prone steel components, pairing thermal spraying with UNSM can extend service life and tailor performance for abrasion, erosion, cavitation, or valve-sealing applications.
method: Deposited WC–Co–Cr coatings by detonation spraying (DS), HVOF, and atmospheric plasma spraying (APS).
Applied ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM) after spraying.
Compared microstructure, hardness, tribology, abrasive/erosive/impact-abrasive/cavitation behavior, corrosion, oxidation, and valve endurance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardness increases up to 1596 HV and the lowest wear metrics for APS+UNSM, while HVOF+UNSM gave the best valve endurance response.
watch_item: The optimal coating is application-specific, so the best lab wear result may not translate directly to the best performance under real service loading or degradation conditions.
paper_title: Ultrasonic Surface Modification of WC-Co-Cr Thermal Spray Coatings: Microstructure, Mechanical Properties and Performance
